Requirement: The platform shall validate experiment manifests against a versioned schema before any work is accepted.
Acceptance measure: Invalid or unknown fields return a stable error and no experiment is created.

Requirement: The platform shall validate dataset manifests and every test case, including unique case IDs, split membership, policy linkage, and content hash.
Acceptance measure: Schema, duplicate, split, and hash tests pass for every promoted dataset.

Requirement: The platform shall compile an immutable expectation record from the approved case, policy, and rubric before target-model execution.
Rationale: Separates policy expectation from response observation.
Acceptance measure: The expectation hash is stored before the provider request and reproduces deterministically.
Risk if omitted: The grader can silently redefine policy.

Requirement: The platform shall expand each accepted experiment into deterministic logical runs keyed by experiment definition, case version, rendered prompt, model configuration, repetition, and lane.
Acceptance measure: Duplicate logical keys are rejected within an experiment; changed inputs change the key.

Requirement: The platform shall execute logical runs through a canonical provider adapter contract while preserving each provider attempt separately.
Rationale: Separates model behavior from provider reliability.
Acceptance measure: Mock and two production adapters pass identical contract fixtures before production.
Release target: MVP mock; production adapters before production

Requirement: The platform shall store rendered requests, terminal responses, provider attempts, expectations, classifications, snapshots, and reports as content-addressed artifacts.
Acceptance measure: Every stored artifact has a verified SHA-256 and project-scoped path.
Risk if omitted: Evidence can be changed without detection.

Requirement: The platform shall classify behavior into appropriate refusal, false refusal, safe useful compliance, unsafe compliance, or ambiguous/partial without treating reliability errors as refusals.
Acceptance measure: Golden fixtures cover all five labels and every reliability terminal state.
Risk if omitted: Safety and helpfulness failures are conflated.

Requirement: The platform shall support grader abstention and route ambiguous, critical, or disputed cases to human review and adjudication.
Rationale: Automation cannot be sole authority for critical cases.
Acceptance measure: Configured escalation rules create review tasks; unresolved critical tasks block publication.
Risk if omitted: Critical errors pass without accountable review.

Requirement: The platform shall compute versioned metric snapshots with explicit numerator, denominator, exclusions, interval method, and exact run population.
Acceptance measure: Golden and mutation tests detect changed denominators and reconcile all counts.

Requirement: The platform shall calculate Wilson intervals and prompt-family cluster bootstrap comparisons using versioned statistical plans.
Rationale: Accounts for uncertainty and correlated prompts.
Acceptance measure: Results match independent reference implementations within approved tolerance.
Release target: Wilson in MVP; cluster bootstrap before production

Requirement: The platform shall evaluate independent raw-metric release gates and critical-event rules before any composite score.
Rationale: Prevents a composite from hiding unsafe compliance.
Acceptance measure: A confirmed unsafe-compliance event blocks; insufficient support yields indeterminate, never pass.
Risk if omitted: Unsafe model can pass an aggregate score.

Requirement: The platform shall generate a signed release dossier containing lineage, metrics, gate checks, unresolved items, costs, and approvals without embedding restricted raw content.
Acceptance measure: Ed25519 signature verifies and report hashes reconcile to stored artifacts.
Risk if omitted: Release decisions cannot be independently reviewed.
Release target: MVP signature; approval bundle before production

Requirement: The platform shall permit regrading stored responses under a new grader version without calling the target model and without overwriting prior classifications.
Acceptance measure: A regrade creates new grader-run and classification records linked by supersession.

Requirement: The platform shall compare candidate and baseline experiments using paired prompt-family analysis and practical regression thresholds.
Rationale: Supports release decisions, not only absolute scores.
Acceptance measure: Comparison report exposes paired deltas, intervals, support, and changed-dataset warnings.

Requirement: The platform shall keep certification, regression, exploration, and monitoring lanes separate in configuration, access, and reporting.
Acceptance measure: A run belongs to exactly one lane; exploration output cannot enter certification snapshots.

Requirement: The platform shall provide CLI and REST interfaces for validate, start, status, pause, resume, cancel, regrade, compare, export, and evidence access workflows.
Acceptance measure: Contract tests verify status codes, idempotency, ETags, and role checks.
Release target: Validate/run/status in MVP; remainder initial release

Requirement: The platform shall enforce budgets for provider cost, grading cost, human-review tasks, storage, and elapsed time before and during execution.
Acceptance measure: Admission rejects impossible budgets; runtime pauses before a hard limit is exceeded.

Requirement: The platform shall capture configured aliases, provider-reported model identifiers, capabilities, and fingerprint canaries for every experiment.
Rationale: Hosted models can drift behind stable aliases.
Acceptance measure: Metadata or canary change raises an alert and marks comparisons pending review.

Requirement: The production API shall achieve at least 99.9% monthly availability excluding approved maintenance.
Acceptance measure: SLO dashboard and monthly error-budget calculation.

Requirement: At least 99.99% of accepted experiment definitions shall remain durably recoverable.
Acceptance measure: Failure-injection and restore tests show no lost accepted experiment.

Requirement: Ninety-five percent of interactive experiments shall begin execution within five minutes when admitted within declared capacity.
Acceptance measure: Queue-age SLI by priority and provider.

Requirement: Ninety-five percent of automated grading shall complete within two minutes after response persistence, excluding human review.
Acceptance measure: Grading-latency histogram meets objective at target load.

Requirement: Ninety-nine percent of reports shall complete within ten minutes after all required metric snapshots are ready.
Acceptance measure: Report-generation SLI and load test.

Requirement: Given frozen artifacts and versioned code, the platform shall reproduce published metric counts and hashes exactly.
Acceptance measure: Reproduction suite yields byte-identical canonical snapshots or a documented deterministic equivalent.

Requirement: The codebase shall maintain at least 80% branch coverage for foundation modules and 100% coverage of gate-critical decision branches.
Rationale: Reduces regression risk in core logic.
Acceptance measure: CI coverage threshold and mutation tests.

Requirement: Production user authentication shall use organization-controlled OIDC with MFA policy inherited from the identity provider.
Acceptance measure: OIDC integration tests cover valid, expired, revoked, and wrong-audience tokens.

Requirement: Authorization shall enforce project scope and role at API, database-row, artifact-prefix, export, and hidden-set boundaries.
Acceptance measure: Negative permission matrix shows no cross-project read or write path.

Requirement: All prompts, outputs, attachments, reports, and notifications shall be rendered as inert data; active HTML, script, external fetch, and executable preview are prohibited by default.
Acceptance measure: Stored-XSS, Markdown, URI, attachment, and export security corpus cannot execute.
Release target: MVP safe HTML; full corpus before production

Requirement: Grading workers shall have no target-provider credentials, no tools, no default external network, and schema-only output.
Acceptance measure: Network and credential canaries remain inaccessible in grader tests.
Risk if omitted: Untrusted output can exfiltrate secrets or act externally.

Requirement: Secrets shall be obtained from a managed secret store, scoped per process and provider, rotated, and never persisted in artifacts, logs, or database payloads.
Acceptance measure: Secret scanners and canary tests detect no persistence; rotation exercise succeeds.

Requirement: Restricted artifacts shall be encrypted in transit and at rest with project- or classification-scoped keys and integrity verification.
Rationale: Harmful content and possible secrets require stronger handling.
Acceptance measure: Key-policy and object-access tests pass; scheduled hash verification is 100%.

Requirement: Every privileged mutation, evidence access, export, approval, override, and policy change shall create an append-only, tamper-evident audit event.
Acceptance measure: Hash-chain verification and tamper test pass; audit outage blocks privileged publication.
Release target: MVP metadata ledger; external checkpoints before production

Requirement: Execution workers shall use explicit outbound allowlists and certification shall use simulators instead of live tools unless an authorized sandbox profile is approved.
Rationale: Prevents evaluations from causing real-world actions.
Acceptance measure: Egress-deny and simulator tests pass; no certification manifest may request live tools by default.

Requirement: The platform shall minimize collection of personal data, secrets, and live identifiers and shall support de-identification before dataset promotion.
Rationale: Benchmarks need content, not unnecessary identities.
Acceptance measure: Dataset promotion rejects prohibited fields and records de-identification status.

Requirement: Each data class shall have an approved retention, deletion, legal-hold, and access-review policy.
Rationale: Immutable evidence does not mean indefinite retention.
Acceptance measure: Lifecycle job, hold precedence, deletion tombstone, and restore behavior are tested.

Requirement: Every score-affecting configuration and artifact shall be versioned and hashed with canonical serialization.
Acceptance measure: Changing any score-affecting field changes the manifest or artifact hash.

Requirement: Every published metric shall expose included runs, excluded runs by reason, numerator, denominator, strict/nominal view, and confidence interval.
Rationale: Prevents silent exclusions and denominator drift.
Acceptance measure: Population reconciliation equations pass for all fixtures.

Requirement: The platform shall preserve a provenance graph from source material through dataset case, rendered request, response, classification, metric snapshot, gate, and dossier.
Acceptance measure: Every graph edge resolves and every referenced hash verifies.

Requirement: Provider metadata used for gating or comparison shall be stored in typed fields; non-critical provider-specific metadata may be JSON.
Rationale: Critical fields must remain queryable and validated.
Acceptance measure: Schema tests reject missing gating metadata and tolerate documented extensions.
Risk if omitted: Provider drift or usage data becomes invisible.

Requirement: Production backups shall support an initial RPO of 15 minutes and RTO of four hours for control-plane state; artifact recovery shall reconcile to all accepted runs.
Acceptance measure: Quarterly restore exercise meets targets and verifies audit/artifact continuity.

Requirement: The platform shall emit structured logs, metrics, traces, and alerts for queue age, provider failures, grading latency, artifact integrity, audit persistence, budget use, and critical labels.
Acceptance measure: Alert tests fire with actionable runbook links and no restricted raw content.
Release target: MVP baseline; production alerts before launch

Requirement: Runbooks shall exist for provider outage, stuck queue, worker death, object-store failure, audit outage, critical unsafe result, backup restore, and signing-key compromise.
Acceptance measure: Game-day exercises complete with recorded evidence and owners.

Requirement: All mutating commands and retryable jobs shall be idempotent; retries shall preserve logical-run identity and create distinct attempt records.
Acceptance measure: Worker-kill and duplicate-request tests produce no duplicate logical runs.
Release target: MVP key; durable worker before production

Requirement: The production web interface shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA for primary evaluation, review, and release workflows.
Rationale: Reviewers must safely use dense evidence interfaces.
Acceptance measure: Automated and manual accessibility audit has no unresolved critical violations.
Risk if omitted: Excludes reviewers and creates legal/operational risk.

Requirement: All primary workflows shall be keyboard operable, expose visible focus, provide non-color status cues, and support screen-reader labels for metrics and review states.
Acceptance measure: Keyboard and assistive-technology test scripts pass.
Risk if omitted: Critical status is inaccessible or ambiguous.

Requirement: No specific regulatory certification is assumed; compliance controls shall remain configurable until jurisdiction, contracts, and data residency are approved.
Acceptance measure: Launch checklist records approved regimes or an explicit no-regime decision.
